source.title: How Far Do SAE Features Persist Across LLM Layers? An Empirical Study with an FFN Pruning Application

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE reconstruction quality and the effect of substituting reconstructions into a forward pass, but in a cross-layer setting and without testing the error structure or comparisons specified by most claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures cross-layer feature carry, FVU, and loss changes from SAE reconstruction substitution. It does not measure linear predictability of reconstruction error, error norms across SAE sizes, or compare reconstruction errors with random errors of the same size. FARN benchmark results concern the proposed pruner, not the claim versions. Rows for cross-layer carry and FVU are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study applies one off-the-shelf layer-24 SAE to deeper layers to measure cross-layer feature carry and to drive FFN pruning (FARN). It never cites or analyses the dark-matter paper. It does not study the SAE error vector's linear predictability, error scaling across SAE sizes, a random-error comparison, or error-term ablation in circuits or steering. Its ΔCE and FVU numbers are mostly for an SAE applied outside its training layer, so they measure cross-layer mismatch rather than the SAE's own error. The relation enum has no exact fit: the paper neither cites nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct but incomplete. The authors' headline is that one SAE keeps firing many of the same features at deeper layers, with family-dependent decay. This cross-layer signal drives a training-free per-prompt FFN pruner (FARN) within 1.5 pp of an activation oracle, beating random, magnitude and calibrated baselines. The ΔCE result is a secondary appendix check showing reconstructions are not functionally interchangeable with deeper residuals.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies one pretrained SAE across deeper layers and evaluates feature persistence, reconstruction fidelity, and a pruning application; it does not use the original study's dark-matter error predictability method.
record.method_sensitivity: Carry and reconstruction fidelity decay differently across TopK, modified-TopK, and JumpReLU SAEs. On Gemma, carry is described as nearly invariant across tested JumpReLU L0 checkpoints while FVU worsens at lower L0.

fits_no_version.finding: A layer-24 SAE's active-feature indices largely persist one layer downstream (carry 0.72–0.82). Decay rate differs by SAE family: JumpReLU keeps about half at +17 layers; TopK drops below half within 5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-layer SAE feature activations transfer to adjacent and deeper layers, at family-dependent rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-layer reconstruction FVU and spliced ΔCE grow with depth in a model- and family-dependent way. ΔCE is already 1.6–2.5 nats at L+1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An SAE's reconstruction fidelity degrades sharply outside its training layer even when feature identification persists.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 9th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: For V3, the study reports loss changes against the clean residual but no random-error comparison matched for size. Persistence uses activation-pattern identity, not semantic feature meaning. Evaluations cover three roughly 8B-scale base models, a single source layer, and downstream accuracy at one neuron budget.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row cap. FARN task accuracy and pruning-signal comparisons are not results about the claim versions; the study's plotted persistence curves beyond the explicitly stated values are not separately transcribed.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation is not measured.
No SAE-size sweep and no per-token error-norm prediction. The Gemma L0 sweep is applied cross-layer and reports only aggregate FVU.
No comparison with random errors of the same norm. ΔCE for in-domain splicing at L24 is not reported.
There is no decomposition of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
There is no circuit or steering analysis with versus without the error term.
There is no architecture or training-objective comparison of in-domain error. SAE family is confounded with model.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V3 link is incorrect. ΔCE here measures applying an SAE outside its training layer, not the pathology of in-domain SAE error relative to norm-matched random error. All rows are therefore relinked to none. SAE family is fully confounded with model (one SAE per model). The dark-matter paper is not cited.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Whether per-token error norms are predictable across SAE sizes, larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and error does not vanish with scale.
The study reports loss increases from substituting SAE reconstructions, but does not compare them with random errors of the same size.
Whether the linear part contains unlearned features and the nonlinear part resists further dictionary learning.
Whether analyses such as circuits or steering lose model behaviour when the SAE error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter is mainly a training artifact and shrinks with different architectures or end-to-end training.
